hints: Notice the question gives only power $25 \, \text{W}$ and p.d. $4.0 \, \text{V}$ across the resistor, so you need the power equation that contains $P$, $V$ and $R$ together.
Recall that for a resistor $P = V^2/R$, so resistance is on the bottom of the fraction and a larger p.d. at fixed power means a larger resistance.
Square the $4.0 \, \text{V}$ to get $16 \, \text{V}^2$, then divide by $25 \, \text{W}$ and check the unit is $\Omega$.
walkthrough: Identify the knowns: power dissipated $P = 25 \, \text{W}$ and p.d. across the resistor $V = 4.0 \, \text{V}$. The unknown is resistance $R$.
State the governing relation for power in a resistor in terms of $V$ and $R$: $P = V^2/R$.
Rearrange for $R$ by multiplying by $R$ and dividing by $P$: $R = V^2/P$.
Substitute with units: $R = (4.0)^2/25 = 16/25$ where numerator is in $\text{V}^2$ and denominator is in $\text{W}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $16/25 = 0.64$, and since $\text{V}^2/\text{W} = \Omega$, $R = 0.64 \, \Omega$.
Match $0.64 \, \Omega$ to the listed options. This is option B.
